question: Why does SaBRe miss loader and shared-object syscalls? Root cause, not symptom.
premise_corrected: The filed premise 'SaBRe rewrites the main ELF and nothing else' is WRONG: the main ELF has ZERO syscall instructions (libc has 525); the four caught syscalls came from libc.so, so SaBRe does rewrite shared objects.

root_cause_1.demonstration: 50 syscalls from a non-allowlisted .so + 50 via libc => sabre intercepts exactly 50/100, ptrace 100/100
root_cause_1.consequence: any app .so with raw syscalls is undeterminized; a Go binary would be almost entirely undeterminized

root_cause_2.what: ld IS rewritten, but its syscalls are routed to real_syscall, bypassing the plugin
root_cause_2.where: loader.c:406-420 rewrites {"ld"}; ld_sc_handler.c:247+ dispatches to real_syscall with the plugin_sc_handler call COMMENTED OUT
root_cause_2.demonstration: dlopen post-startup: ptrace sees openat/mmap/mprotect, sabre sees none => scope+routing, not timing

fix_machinery_already_present: hide_sbr_maps tracks SaBRe's own segments (self-exclusion solved)
calling_from_plugin re-entrancy guard already at top of ld_sc_handler
no_fix_attempted: vendored third-party GPL-3.0 C under a build.rs-asserted REVISION marker; root cause 2 was deliberately disabled by someone
